-A-N_cazqpw.description:
In today’s vlog, we are going for our Snorkelling Tour in Nusa Penida — the same one we booked yesterday (you can check all booking details in my last vlog).
We started our morning with the Manta Ray Snorkelling Tour where we were supposed to see the beautiful Mantas in the ocean… and yes, we did see them — but the experience was not what we expected.
On our way, the ocean waves were extremely rough. Our boat was very small, with no railings, and it was jumping up and down due to the tide.
Honestly, we were scared and for a moment, it felt like we could drown.
When we finally reached the Manta point — the mantas were SO beautiful… calm, majestic and so gentle.
But the reality is, the water here is too heavy and rough for safe snorkelling, and we realized that by going in such strong currents, we might be harming the animals and risking ourselves.
This vlog contains our honest review and experience of this tour.
If you are planning Nusa Penida — please watch this part carefully before deciding. 🥺⚠️
After the tour, we went to Bubu Beach, enjoyed a peaceful beach dip and had our lunch there — and that part really made our day lighter and happier again. 🌊✨
Hope you enjoy the vlog & take something helpful from it ❤️
Don’t forget to Like, Share & Subscribe for the upcoming Nusa Penida adventures 🌴

**Uluwatu Temple and Kecak Dance**

Uluwatu Temple is one of Bali’s most famous sea temples, located on a high cliff overlooking the Indian Ocean. It is dedicated to the sea spirits and offers stunning sunset views.

The Kecak Dance is a traditional Balinese performance held at Uluwatu during sunset. It features a large group of men chanting “cak-cak-cak” in unison, telling the story of the Ramayana epic with dramatic fire and dance scenes.

2hJEAySptME.description:
"Kecak is a form of Balinese dance and music drama that was developed in the 1930s in Bali, Indonesia.
Also known as the Ramayana Monkey Chant, the piece, performed by a circle of at least 70-100 performers wearing checked cloth around their waists, percussively chanting "can" and moving their hands and arms, depicts a battle from the Ramayana. The monkey-like Vanara led by Hanuman helped Prince Rama fight the evil King Ravana. Kecak has roots in sanghyang, a trance-inducing exorcism dance."
I watched kecak dance twice and the best one was at Uluwatu Temple during the sunset. 
Here is some footage from the performance that I watched in February 2017.

___________________________________________________________________

Kecak dance é um drama Balines que mistura de dança e música que foi desenvolvida nos anos 30 em Bali, Indonésia. 
Também conhecida como Canto do Macaco Ramayana, a peça apresentada em circulo por uma media de 70-100 participantes usando roupas até a cintura, cantando "can" e movendo as mãos e os braços, representa a luta de Ramayana. 
Vanara, que tem aparência de macaco, e liderado por Hanumam, ajuda o Príncipe Rana a lutar contra o demônio do Rei Ravana.
Kecak tem raízes no "sanghyang", uma dança que induz ao exorcismo. 
Eu assisti duas apresentações da Dança Kecak, e a melhor foi durante o pôr-do-sol no Temple Uluwatu.
Aqui um pouco das imagens gravadas em fevereiro de 2017.

403eFJj3Mb4.description:
Today we visit Sekumpul Waterfall, the highest waterfall in Bali. It is located in the north of the island, somewhat hidden in a valley.

The most beautiful and highest waterfall in Bali "Sekumpul" is located north of the central lakes Danau Bratan and Danau Buyan (Bedugul). A narrow mountain road leads from the main road to the starting point of the short hiking tour. The journey alone is an experience; on a clear day you can see all the way to the coast. Sekumpul Waterfall is actually made up of seven separate waterfalls, all relatively close to each other. The highest of these waterfalls is around 80 meters high, while the others are around 40-50 meters high. This beautiful area, which is very popular with tourists, is located in Sekumpul Village Municipality in Buleleng District.

A guide is required to descend to the waterfall. From him we learn a lot of interesting facts about the region, the waterfalls and also the people who live here. And he also gives us one or two photo and film tips.

The path into the valley is steep and involves many stairs. At the beginning we walk through small farms, but then there is only the impressive tropical nature. From here you have fantastic views of the various waterfalls, the sound of which accompanies our hike. After about 30 minutes we reach the bottom. There is now only a river between the waterfall and us, but there is no bridge here! But crossing the river is easily manageable because the current is not strong and now in the dry season the water barely reaches our knees.

We first go to the Hidden Waterfall. It is so named because it is not visible from above and is located slightly away from the other waterfalls. We reach a small valley basin. The green overgrown rock walls and the contrast of the spraying waterfall look like something from a fairy tale world.
Then we continue to the actual Sekumpul waterfall. We repeatedly wade through small streams and climb over wet, slippery rocks. Bathing shoes are an advantage here. But the majestic sight rewards us for our efforts. With a drop of 80 meters, Sekumpul Waterfall is a spectacular scene. You can also swim in the pool. The water is surprisingly quite cold, even though we are in the tropics.
Finally we go to the three Fiji waterfalls. These fall over numerous rocks into the valley and the spray forms a kind of mist, which, together with the green vegetation and the rocks, creates a magical atmosphere. Without the other tourists, you would feel like you were in a dense jungle far from civilization.

Wet but enthusiastic, we start our way back, which now takes us back up the many stairs. This is much more strenuous than the descent, but it's done after 45 minutes.

On the way back we pass a viewpoint over Lake Tamblingan that we visited a few days ago. https://youtu.be/lBSFjyBBRgU?si=3VP_o1sU10tNC6k0

Here in the parking lot there are lots of monkeys, the ubiquitous long-tailed macaques, waiting for the tourists' treats.

If you enjoyed it, please like and subscribe to the channel so you don't miss anything.

4gNw3W5GBwk.description:
🌴 7 Things NOT to Do in Bali – A Tourist Survival Guide 🇮🇩

Planning your Bali escape? 🏝️ Before you pack your bags and bikinis, make sure you avoid these common tourist mistakes to keep your trip smooth, fun, and safe! 👇

⸻

1. 🚱 Don’t Drink Tap Water

Bali’s tap water isn’t safe for drinking — even brushing your teeth with it can cause issues. Stick to bottled or filtered water to avoid Bali belly. 💦

⸻

2. 🛵 Don’t Ride a Scooter Without Experience

Bali’s roads can be chaotic. If you’re not confident on a scooter, skip it. Always wear a helmet and carry an international license or risk accidents and police fines.

⸻

3. 🛕 Don’t Disrespect Local Culture

Temples are sacred spaces. Always wear a sarong, cover your shoulders, and never disturb ceremonies. Respect earns smiles here 😊🙏

⸻

4. 🐒 Don’t Tease the Monkeys

They may look cute in Ubud Monkey Forest, but they steal glasses, phones, and snacks! 😅 Avoid feeding or provoking them.

⸻

5. 💸 Don’t Use Dodgy Money Changers

Those offering “too good” rates often scam tourists. Use official, air-conditioned counters, and count your cash before leaving.

⸻

6. 🦟 Don’t Forget Mosquito Protection

Dengue fever is real. Always use repellent, especially at sunset, and wear long sleeves in jungle areas.

⸻

7. 🍹 Don’t Drink Cheap Arak

Unregulated arak can be toxic. Only drink at trusted bars or resorts. Better safe than sorry!

⸻

✨ Respect Bali, stay aware, and this magical island will reward you with unforgettable memories! 🌅💃🌺

#NusaPenida #NusaLembongan #ScubaDiving #DiveConcepts #BestDiveSites
Dive into the best dive sites in Nusa Penida while staying on Nusa Lembongan and diving with Dive Concepts! Explore Crystal Bay, famous for its crystal-clear waters and seasonal mola mola (sunfish); Manta Point, where majestic manta rays glide effortlessly year-round; and SD Point, PED, and Buyuk, offering vibrant coral reefs and exhilarating drift dives. Experience the rich biodiversity of Toyapakeh, a diver-favorite with stunning coral gardens and abundant marine life. Follow me in my video exploring these top dive sites and discover why Nusa Penida is a must-visit destination for every scuba diver!
Diving in Nusa Penida offers an incredible variety of marine life, from the famous manta rays at Manta Point to the elusive mola mola (sunfish) at Crystal Bay during the season. Drift along vibrant coral reefs at SD Point, PED, and Buyuk, where you'll spot schools of trevally, sweetlips, and fusiliers, as well as colorful nudibranchs hidden among the corals. Toyapakeh is a hotspot for reef sharks, turtles, and stunning soft corals, while lucky divers might even encounter bamboo sharks, wobbegongs, or the rare rhinopias (lacey scorpionfish). Keep an eye out for ornate ghost pipefish, frogfish, and the mesmerizing blue-ringed octopus hiding in the reef. With strong currents bringing in pelagic life, Nusa Penida is a paradise for macro lovers and big fish enthusiasts alike!

For the adventurous, Sekumpul promises an intimate connection with the natural splendor of Bali.

Fiji Falls: Another must-have Fiji Falls in Bali, with powerful waterfalls and crystal clear water. Whether you’re diving or just scuba diving, Fiji Falls is an adventure lover’s paradise. Vibrant foliage and refreshing murmurs make this a haven for nature lovers.

For the ultimate waterfall experience, don’t miss Tegenungan Falls, one of Bali’s most famous waterfalls and the highlight of any Ubud trip, Tegenungan, which runs from the center of Ubud is short, surrounded by lush forests, making it one of the best waterfalls in the area.

If you are planning a visit to Bali waterfalls, be sure to include Tibumana and Gitgit waterfalls which are known for their pristine waters and stunning surroundings Ubud's waterfalls, in particular hidden gems like Fiji and Sekumpull, are one of the best things to do in Bali.

This Bali Airport international arrivals guide takes you through how to deal with the Indonesia arrival card, visa on arrival process, customs checks, baggage collection and transfers in Denpasar. It also covers the Bali Airport arrival process at I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport so travellers can understand each step before landing.

Bali Airport arrivals can feel busy after a long international flight, so what should you expect? What are the best tips and tricks? This walkthrough guide shows the full Bali Airport arrivals process at I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport in Denpasar, including key steps that appear in most Bali Airport arrivals guides and Denpasar Airport arrivals information for international travellers.

The POV walkthrough covers how to fill out the Indonesia Arrival Card form for Australians and all travellers, the Indonesia arrival form online option, the visa on arrival system — also known as e‑VOA when completed before departure — customs checks, baggage collection and the transport choices available once you exit the terminal. This includes Bali Airport transfers and the rideshare service Grab. Everything is shown through clear POV footage so you can understand the layout and sequence before you land.

The video begins at the aerobridge and follows the route into the main arrivals corridor. You’ll see where the Indonesia Arrival Card can be completed if not done before you leave, how the digital form works and what information you need to have ready. The walkthrough also shows how the arrival card form works for travellers entering Bali, including the online Indonesia arrival form and how to fill the arrival card Bali version as part of the standard arrivals process at Denpasar Airport.

The guide explains the difference between the standard visa on arrival and the e‑VOA, including queue lengths, payment methods and the order of each step at I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport visa on arrival counters. The walkthrough covers the full Bali visa on arrival process at the airport, including the queue layout, payment steps, the Bali visa on arrival application, how the counters operate at I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport, and how to get visa on arrival in Bali when arriving on an international flight.

Inside the arrivals hall, the video shows how customs screening works, what officers typically check and how to prepare your bags. The baggage claim area is included in full, with signage, carousel layout and practical tips for families travelling with children or multiple suitcases. This includes trolleys. You’ll also see the shops and services available before exiting the terminal, including eSIM card counters, ATMs, cafés and small convenience stores.

These elements are all part of the typical Denpasar Airport arrivals experience, from Denpasar Airport arrivals maps and Bali Airport arrivals information through to the standard Denpasar Airport customs procedures travellers move through before exiting the terminal.

Once outside, the guide explains how to find your hotel transfer, where drivers usually wait and how to locate the Grab pickup area. This section includes real‑world crowd levels, wayfinding and advice on avoiding common bottlenecks. Families will find guidance on keeping the process manageable with kids, including where to pause, where to regroup and how to handle the heat after stepping outside. This aligns with Bali with Kids planning and Bali family travel research.

This arrivals guide is part of my wider Indonesia travel series and connects directly to my Bali with Kids content, which includes resort reviews, attraction guides, itineraries and practical travel advice for families visiting the island. You’ll find related videos on airport departures, Ubud itineraries, Waterbom Bali, temple visits, beach areas and family‑friendly resorts across the island.

I’m Chris Stead, an award‑winning journalist, travel editor and creator of the Motivated Travel Show. I produce premium, honest, cinematic travel reviews and guides designed to help you travel smarter, better and with more confidence across Australia, Asia and beyond.

This video is part of my Indonesia travel series and my Bali with Kids series. You’ll find more Bali Airport arrivals guides, resort walkthroughs and family travel guides across the channel.

We're super excited to share with you all the Season Two finale of Early Weekends! 
Presenting the entrancing Kecak Dance, performed at the iconic Uluwatu Temple in Bali, Indonesia.

The Kecak Dance performance is a time-honoured tradition which offers a glimpse into Balinese culture and mythology, as the performers tell ancient stories through the unique fusion of vocals, rhythmic chants and captivating movements.

Based on the Hindu epic "Ramayana", Prince Rama's wife, Princess Sita, is abducted by the demon king Ravana. The dance depicts the dramatic battle scenes between Prince Rama and the army of monkeys led by Hanuman, as they attempt to rescue Princess Sita and defeat the evil Ravana.

Thanks so much to everyone for joining throughout our second season, we've had a blast being able to showcase some of the amazing music on the wonderful Sunshine Coast!

BUT DON'T FRET! The season finale of Early Weekends is JUST THE BEGINNING!

DhdPwlvRwF4.description:
in todays bali travel video vlog I visit bali international airport where I provide you with a guide and tour around bali international airport and share all the information you will need to know if you are arriving in bali for the very first time. money changers, atm machines, how to obtain a sim card, tourist tax levy,  and getting a taxi from the airport/harris hotel to your hotel stay in bali. all information provided in this video is current 2026 information.

VIDEO CONTENT: A guide to bali international airport for first time visitors to bali. information provided in this video on money changers, sim cards/data packages/taxi.

WHO IS THIS VIDEO FOR: this video will offer a useful guide to bali international airport for those whom are first time visitors to Bali, Indonesia. this video will provide all the information you need to know for all budget types and offer an in-depth guide of what to expect upon arrival to bali international airport in 2026

MONEY CHANGERS: there are now 4 money changers within the arrivals hall at the international airport all offer exactly the same exchange rates with no commission charges. money exchange rates at the airport are lower than the money exchange rates that you will find at the street money changers in all the popular tourist areas. 

MONEY CHANGERS: Mandiri, Bri, Bni, Btn

ATM MACHINES: you will find many atm machines located next to all the money changers.

SIM CARD: There are 4 different companies in the international airport arrivals hall offering sim cards & data packages where prices start from 250,000idr. 

4 TELECOMMUNICATIONS COMPANIES: XL, Telcomsel, IM3, Smartfren 

OPERATING HOURS OF SIM CARD PROVIDERS: XL STAFF ADVISED ME THAT OPERATION HOURS ARE 07:00AM-03:00AM.

all international tourists arriving in bali whom wish to use internet whilst travelling around bali will be required to purchase an indonesian sim card. registration of the sim card is required by the company whom you purchase your sim card from, the company will require access to your phone device to install the sim card and register the card, this process will take a maximum of 5 minutes.

CAN I PURCHASE A SIM CARD OUTSIDE OF THE AIRPORT: it is possible to purchase a sim card outside of the airport however this can sometimes be a little difficult to find because many places sell sim cards but cannot complete the registration process, at the airport you are dealing direct with the telecommunications providers. 

PURCHASING SIM CARD FROM THE STREET: you must be very careful if you decide to purchase a sim card data package from the street as in most instances the deal may seem better on the street than what is on offer at the airport but this is not usually the case as packages bought from the street will not be unlimited packages (unless same price as in airport) it will be split data.

Uluwatu in Bali attracts every visitor because of its multiple tourist attractions like the famous Uluwatu dance ( Ramayana dance) plus it also has some of the famous sea beaches of Bali.

Apart from exploring Uluwatu temple we also had local warung food in Uluwatu Bali and enjoyed the taste of Nasi Campur.

Just in case you have missed watching our 5th episode of the Bali Series - Nusa Penida, Sea beaches of Nusa Penida along with water sports activities like Snorkelling. You may check the below link.

https://youtu.be/tl3u8IqPBZY?si=mnIULZx-1mqy2v3j

Following are the details of places visited by us 

Uluwatu Temple & Kecak Dance - There are two dance shows in evening, we saw the first one and that was a  better choice.- 6 pm and 7 pm ( show duration approx 45 min)
Overall, It was an amazing experience to see the Kecak Dance here in Uluwatu along with temple visit.

Word of caution - Monkeys at Uluwatu temple are very aggressive, so keep hands free of any food related stuff.

Uluwatu Temple Tickets - 50,000 IDR (260 INR) Per Person
Kecak Dance Tickets - 10,00,00 IDR (500 INR) Per Person
After this, we ended our day here in Uluwatu, BTW we reached Uluwatu from Nusa Penida.

Next Morning - 25th March 

Suluban Beach -  This beach is famous for the Surfing. Here you can also hire a surfing board on a rent on an hourly basis. 

Padang Padang Beach - 3 km from Suluban beach.
Padang Padang Beach Tickets - 15,000 IDR (80 INR) Per Person entry ticket.

Rainy Season in Bali - December to February
Best Time to visit Bali - April to August 

If you are coming to Bali between July to Sept so you have to come with the Pre-Booking. Plus there is lot of traffic.

Lunch at Yeye's Warung ( Restaurant)  - We had Nasi Campur for lunch,in this restaurant you can prepare your Nasi Campur on your own.

Tempeh & Tofu is popular in Bali, we had it here as well, just in case if you have missed watchin video about how Tempeh and Tofu is made you can check the below video:

https://youtu.be/zMXvIuz7KFI?si=RkC4Mj8CFjRJ2pcw

Pandawa Beach - After lunch we travelled for around 30 minutes & reached at the one more Sea Beach of Uluwatu is “Pandawa Beach”. 
We did Kayaking here & enjoyed it.

Kayaking Charge - Rs 500 INR

Kuta Beach Sunset - After this, we travelled for 20 km and reached at the “Kuta Beach” for Sunset & ended our day.

Uluwatu Temple: Bali's Sacred Clifftop Marvel and Enchanting Sunset

🌅 Welcome to our channel, where we're about to embark on an incredible journey to the awe-inspiring Uluwatu Temple in Bali, Indonesia! Perched majestically on dramatic cliffs overlooking the Indian Ocean, this ancient sea temple is not only a symbol of Bali's rich heritage but also a place of breathtaking natural beauty.

🏛️ Discover the history and legends surrounding Uluwatu, dating back to the 11th century, and witness the captivating Kecak and Fire Dance performances that bring tales from the Ramayana epic to life.

GL6kmkHrNmE.description:
The emerald-green rice terraces in the river gorge north of Tegallalang village (sometimes also spelled as Tegalalang), around 9 kilometres from Ubud centre, are photography-wise probably the most famous rice fields in Bali. The cool and breezy area has a vista that spreads out in front of you in the form of rice terraces all over the slopes across the timeless valley. The beautiful Tegalalang Rice Terrace is actually an ancient irrigation system, dating back to the eighth century. From Kuta it is just a 1,5 hour drive away and the location is easy to find.

Most people who have visited Bali say that the real Bali can be found where the rice grows. In Bali rice fields can be found almost everywhere, and the Balinese people have depended on this method of agriculture for almost 2000 years. The terraced rice fields were carved by hand, with the help of some simple tools, and are being maintained by succeeding generations. Imagine yourself watching the sun rise through the mist over a rice field or taking a hike through their lush greenness. It is a must thing to do in Bali to visit at least one of the numerous rice paddies.

GmW6Bc7U9cc.description:
📍 Pura Besakih, Mother Temple Bali

Ever dreamt of visiting Bali but worried you wouldn’t get an authentic experience because it’s so popular? We visited the island’s LARGEST temple during one of the BIGGEST celebrations in Bali, and there was no better way to learn about and immerse ourselves into the culture of this island and its people.

🗓️ Once a year (usually during March/April) the Balinese celebrate Galangun, a special holiday honouring the victory of dharma (good) over adharma (evil). 

🙏 Travelling to Bali during this time and soaking in how the whole island celebrates is one of the most special travel experiences you can have. 

☁️ Did you know Bali is called the “Island of the Gods" 🫶 because of the strong spiritual connection that the Balinese people have with Hinduism and the many temples across the island.

🌏 Everything must look beautiful and clean during Galangun as Balinese Hindu’s believe God’s come to down to visit the Earth!

✨ This means dressing the temples, cleaning the streets, placing offerings outside homes - Bali must look visually appealing and welcoming.

🛕 Over 21 days, EVERY person who practices Balinese Hinduism will attempt to visit Besakih Great Temple, the most important, largest and holiest temple in Balinese Hinduism.

💰 Entrance is £3 ($3.70) and includes a private tour with a local guide (which completely makes the experience) - no need to pre-book, just arrive!

Hra23zCNymA.description:
This is my final video from Bali, and I’m spending the last day exploring the stunning Uluwatu region.
The journey begins at Pandawa Cliffs, walking between massive limestone walls before reaching Pandawa Beach, one of the most scenic beaches in southern Bali.
Next, I head to Melasti Beach, a perfect spot for swimming with clear water and dramatic coastal views. After some time by the sea, I take a break at Meladani Café, enjoying food and drinks with an incredible cliffside atmosphere.
To end the day, I explore Uluwatu Temple, perched high above the Indian Ocean. As the sun sets, I finish this Bali journey by watching the iconic Kecak Dance, performed against one of the most breathtaking sunset backdrops in the world.
A perfect farewell to Bali.

✨ Ferry departs from: Ferry departs from Bali to Nusa Penida, from the following locations.

🚤 Sanur is the most convenient port of departure because it is near tourist centers in Bali and there are plenty of operators. Takes about 45 minutes.
🚤 Kusamba has frequent service too but it sort of off the tourist route. Takes about 40 minutes.
🚤 Padang Bai is interesting for those who want to take their own vehicle to the island. The public car ferry service leaves from here but it is not very dependable.

▶️ So, we suggest taking the fast boat from Sanur.

At Nusa Penida:
There are 3 landing ports on Nusa Penida: Buyuk boat landing, Toya Pakeh boat pier (also referred to as Banjar Nyuh), and Sampalan boat landing, based on the ferry provider, the landing may differ.

⏰ Timings:
1st boat to Nusa Penida: 7 am
Last boat from Nusa Penida: 5 pm

✨ PRO TIP: Return tickets at more economical than a single journey fare.

📋 To book:

1️⃣ Online via klook or other booking sites (Cost starts at INR 788 / USD 9.5)
2️⃣ Walk-in at the port

📣 For Day trips:
There are boats for designated places, like a boat to Angel’s Billabong, so on and so forth, so based on your itinerary, you can select.

💡 Stay vs Day trip:
If you plan to explore the island well, it is recommended to stay and explore at your place. The island is best and too beautiful to rush as a day trip there.

Mount Batur sunrise trekking is an extraordinary adventure that should not be missed when visiting Bali. Great for solo, couples and groups.
This is a fantastic way to go back to see natural scenery, having fun with the fresh air and releasing stress from your mind.
This is an moderate level trek, which takes about 2 to 3 hours to get to the peak.  A bit of challenge but worth it, plus the thrill of hiking an active volcano with UNESCO status.
With its stunning sunrise over Lake Batur and Mount Agung, this hike offers a once in a lifetime opportunity to witness the natural beauty of Bali.
By booking a trekking package that includes a guide and transportation, hikers can ensure a safe and enjoyable experience. The experienced guides are familiar with the trail and provide valuable insights along the way. They also assist hikers in navigating the challenging sections of the trek. 
Safety precautions, such as hiring a local guide and being aware of weather conditions, are essential to make the most of this adventure.
Be prepared with comfortable hiking shoes, appropriate clothing, and enough water to stay hydrated. Whether you are an avid trekker or simply a nature enthusiast, the Mount Batur sunrise trek will leave you in awe of Bali’s stunning landscapes. 
The sense of accomplishment after completing the hike and the mesmerizing views from the summit make it a truly unforgettable experience. 
So, make sure to include this thrilling adventure on your Bali itinerary and create memories that will last a lifetime.

So many details go into planning a trip to Nusa Penida, especially if you (like us) aren't comfortable driving a motorbike. Figuring out all of the little details, like cars to port, ferries to and from the island, cars to all of the gorgeous sights, and the snorkeling once you get to the island felt overwhelming. Especially when we were getting mixed reviews from friends in our hostel about whether Nusa Penida is even worth it! 

So we decided to book this tour with Viator to do all of the top things in Nusa Penida in 1 Day (and have it all figured out FOR US!). We booked this tour via the Chase Travel Portal to earn 5x miles using our Chase Sapphire Preferred. 

Our Tour: 
https://www.viator.com/tours/Seminyak/One-Day-Nusa-Penida-Island-West/d34198-112335P1?pid=P00130253&mcid=42383&medium=link 

Our Favorite Tours:
https://www.viator.com/partner-shop/madventure/?medium=link&medium_version=shop

Shop Our Travel Essentials & Camera Gear at our Amazon Storefront: https://amazon.com/shop/madventure 

The day started with a car arriving to our hostel in Canggu, Bali, Indonesia at sunrise to take us to the ferry port, we ferried to the island of Nusa Penida and were immediately directed to another boat for a snorkel tour! Snorkeling with Manta Rays was what Ivan was most excited about for his birthday trip, and wow it was so unbelievable! Next we visited three more snorkel spots, Crystal Bay, Manta Bay, and Gamat Bay where we saw so many beautiful fish including angel fish and barracudas! 

Back on land we ended up on a private tour, where our guide drove us to Kelingking Beach, one of the most social media famous spots in the world. After a quick lunch, we proceeded to Broken Beach and Angel's Billabong. All absolutely gorgeous, and then we caught the ferry back to Bali and the car back to our hostel. Everything but the food itself was included in our tour, making for such an easy day full of hard core travel! We highly recommend this tour!

Hi guys. My Longest travel vlog yet! And our longest journey as a family.

I hope you enjoy coming along with us.

Here is our Bali 13 night itinerary:

First stop - 4 nights in Kuta -
It's close to the airport, but definitely not the nicest part of Bali. We honeymooned here so stayed at Alaya Dedaun (https://alayahotels.com/alayadedaunkuta/) for 4 nights to reminisce, we relaxed in our villa to recover from our long journey and went to places like Seminyak and Jimbaran Bay for dinner. You could stay here or Seminyak/Jimbaran Bay for a couple of nights then move on. Beaches around here are good for surfing. 

Second Stop Ubud - 4 nights 
We found an independent villa rental, Casa Pohon (https://casapohonubud.id-indonesia.com/en/) and it was magical. We used this as a base as we went exploring every day. They provided a car and driver/tour guide for around £45/$60 for a full day. 
Great for: Bali Swing Danau Baratan Jatiluwih Rice Terrace Kemenuh Butterfly park Numerous temples and some great jungle pool bars to end our days - one even overlooked the Tegenungan waterfall. 

3rd stop Mara River Safari lodge for 1 night 
https://www.marariversafarilodge.com/
Such a unique experience. Our main reason to visit was for the giraffe breakfast and it did not disappoint. Spaces are very limited and can only be booked on arrival- so my advice is arrive early on check in day and make it the first thing you book when you arrive. 

4th stop - 4 nights Nusa Dua Beach 
We stayed at the Melia hotel and it’s pretty special. You can go all inclusive which is probably best if you’re not going to venture out much. The beach is great and the kids activities are good. It could be anywhere in the world I suppose but a nice relaxing end to an eventful trip.

WhGU4pEl6rk.description:
Discover Besakih Temple, the Mother Temple of Bali, a sacred complex that sits high on the slopes of Mount Agung, Bali’s tallest and most revered volcano. As the island’s largest and holiest Hindu temple, Besakih is not just a place of worship—it is the spiritual heart of Bali, where faith, tradition, and breathtaking landscapes come together.

In this video, we explore the history, architecture, and spiritual significance of Besakih Temple. From its layered stone terraces and panoramic mountain views to the vibrant ceremonies that unite the Balinese community, Besakih offers a glimpse into the soul of the island.

Balinese Hinduism is unique compared to Indian Hinduism. While rooted in the same Vedic traditions, it blends Hindu philosophy with local beliefs and ancestor worship. Unlike India, where Hinduism is vast and diverse, Balinese Hinduism is more localized, deeply tied to village life, seasonal ceremonies, and offerings that maintain balance between the spiritual and earthly realm. They worship Trimurti or Ishwara, the supreme God is One. It was exciting for me to know all about it. 

Whether you’re planning a trip to Bali or simply curious about its rich culture, this guide will help you understand why Besakih Temple is a must-visit destination.

Planning four days in Bali but feeling overwhelmed by endless Instagram spots and conflicting recommendations? This tropical paradise offers everything from pristine beaches to ancient temples, but most visitors miss the authentic experiences that make Bali truly special.
This video shows exactly how to experience the best of Bali without missing the hidden gems locals prefer to keep to themselves. We're covering Ubud's cultural heart, the best beaches for every type of traveler, secret waterfalls, where to eat like a local, and the crucial mistakes that can ruin your Bali experience.
This is how to spend four days in Bali. Let's dive in!

Day 1: "Get Your Bearings in Ubud"
Rise early for a stress-free airport arrival. The international airport in Denpasar gets increasingly busy as the day progresses, so having transportation pre-arranged is essential. A private driver costs around twenty to twenty-three US dollars for the ninety-minute journey to Ubud. Book through reputable companies like Grab or GoJek rather than accepting random airport taxi offers to avoid being overcharged.
Start your Ubud exploration with a traditional Balinese breakfast at Warung Biah Biah, where dishes like bubur ayam, chicken rice porridge, or nasi campur, mixed rice, will cost around two US dollars. This local favorite opens at seven in the morning and offers authentic flavors without tourist pricing.
By mid-morning, when most tourists are still arriving, head to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary. Arriving before ten in the morning lets you enjoy this natural reserve with over twelve hundred macaques without the crowds. The weekday entrance fee is about seven US dollars per person. Keep valuables secure and avoid carrying food – these monkeys are skilled pickpockets! The sanctuary takes about ninety minutes to explore fully.
For lunch, escape the tourist zone and visit Warung Nia, located ten minutes north of the Monkey Forest. Their crispy duck sets, called bebek goreng, for about four US dollars offer incredible value and authentic flavors that larger restaurants can't match.
In the afternoon, visit the Tegallalang Rice Terraces while most tourists are still in central Ubud. These UNESCO-recognized terraces showcase Bali's ancient subak irrigation system. The main entrance fee is about two US dollars per person. For the best photographs, arrive before three in the afternoon when the light creates stunning shadows across the terraced landscape.
Don't miss the chance to try a Bali swing experience – but skip the overpriced tourist spots charging over thirty US dollars. Instead, visit the family-run Aloha Swing, where ten US dollars gets you unlimited swings, a welcome drink, and breathtaking views without the Instagram queues.
As evening approaches, head to the Ubud Art Market, known as Pasar Seni Ubud. After five in the evening, vendors are more willing to negotiate, and you can find handcrafted souvenirs for thirty to fifty percent less than daytime prices. Practice your bargaining skills – start at forty percent of their initial asking price and meet in the middle.
For dinner, experience a traditional Balinese feast at Warung Pulau Kelapa. Their rijsttafel sampling menu lets you try multiple authentic dishes for about eight US dollars per person. Make reservations in advance as this hidden gem fills quickly with in-the-know travelers.
End your first day with a traditional dance performance at the Ubud Palace, Puri Saren Agung. The Legong and Barong performances start at seven-thirty in the evening, lasting about ninety minutes for around seven US dollars per person. Arrive thirty minutes early to secure good seats, as these authentic cultural performances sell out nightly.
Tomorrow we'll leave the cultural heart of Bali behind and discover the island's breathtaking natural wonders – including a sunrise hike that few travelers experience but everyone remembers forever.

Day 2: "Adventure Day"
Begin with a two in the morning wake-up call for the Mount Batur sunrise trek – yes, it's early, but absolutely worth it! Book through a reputable company like Bali Sunrise Trekking for around thirty US dollars per person, which includes hotel pickup, guide, flashlights, and breakfast at the summit. The moderate two-hour climb is suitable for average fitness levels, though proper footwear is essential as the volcanic terrain can be loose and slippery.
From the summit at seventeen hundred meters, witness a spectacular sunrise over Lake Batur and Mount Agung in the distance.

Y5RyQL7AVng.description:
Discover the spiritual heart of Bali at Besakih Temple, also known as the Mother Temple! 🛕 

Nestled on the sacred slopes of Mount Agung, this magnificent complex is the largest and holiest temple on the island, with a rich history stretching back over 1,000 years. 🌋 

The temple complex consists of 23 individual temples, each dedicated to various deities, with Pura Penataran Agung standing as the most significant. 

Besakih Temple is a living symbol of the “Tri Hita Karana” philosophy, which emphasizes harmony with 
1. With nature
2. With fellow humans
3. With the spiritual realm 

In 1963, Mount Agung erupted, and though much of the surrounding area was devastated, the temple was miraculously spared, symbolizing divine protection. 🌄 

Whether you visit during the vibrant Odalan festival or for a quiet moment of reflection, Besakih Temple is a source of inspiration for those on a spiritual and entrepreneurial journey. ✨

Mount Batur
Mount Batur (Gunung Batur) is an active volcano located at the center of two concentric calderas north west of Mount Agung on the island of Bali, Indonesia. The south east side of the larger 10×13 km caldera contains a caldera lake. The inner 7.5-kilometer-wide caldera, which was formed during emplacement of the Bali (or Ubud) ignimbrite, has been dated at about 23,670 and 28,500 years ago.

baCqr0c8iYc.description:
Besakih Great Temple is the largest and holiest Hindu temple complex in Bali. It is located on the southwestern slopes of Mount Agung, the island’s highest volcano. The site consists of more than 80 individual temples arranged across multiple terraces.

The complex is often called the “Mother Temple” of Balinese Hinduism. Religious ceremonies are held regularly and can involve large pilgrimages from across the island. The temples date back at least to the early medieval period, with roots possibly earlier. The architecture is characterized by tiered meru towers and split gates typical of Balinese temple design.

byvOd4-icKE.description:
One of the most awe-inspiring snorkeling experiences in Bali can be found at Manta Bay in Nusa Penida, where encounters with majestic manta rays leave visitors in awe.

Bali, the famed Indonesian island known for its natural beauty and cultural charm, is a haven for adventure seekers and nature enthusiasts. While Bali is renowned for its picturesque landscapes and vibrant culture, it is also home to an extraordinary underwater world that captivates snorkelers from around the globe. 

Located just a short boat ride from Bali's southeastern coast, Nusa Penida is a small island that offers some of the best snorkeling and diving opportunities in the region. Among its many remarkable snorkeling spots, Manta Bay stands out as a must-visit destination for marine life enthusiasts. Manta Bay, also known as Manta Point, is celebrated for its abundant population of manta rays, which gather in these waters to feed and be cleaned by small fish.

Setting off from the shores of Nusa Penida, snorkelers embark on an exciting journey to Manta Bay. As they venture into the crystal-clear waters, a sense of anticipation builds, knowing that they are about to encounter one of the most graceful creatures in the ocean. Manta rays, with their large wingspans and gentle demeanor, create a truly mesmerizing spectacle as they glide effortlessly through the water.

Upon arriving at Manta Bay, snorkelers are greeted by an underwater vista teeming with life. The visibility is often exceptional, allowing visitors to fully appreciate the breathtaking sight of manta rays gracefully swimming beneath them. Snorkelers can observe these magnificent creatures from a respectful distance, marveling at their elegance and the gentle flapping of their wings as they glide effortlessly through the water.

In addition to the manta rays, Manta Bay is home to a diverse range of marine life. Vibrant coral formations serve as a backdrop for an array of tropical fish, including colorful angelfish, parrotfish, and butterflyfish. Snorkelers may even catch a glimpse of other fascinating marine creatures such as sea turtles, reef sharks, and various species of reef fish.

To fully enjoy the experience, it is recommended to join a guided snorkeling tour led by experienced instructors who can provide insights into the marine life and ensure the safety of participants. These knowledgeable guides are familiar with the behavior of the manta rays and can lead snorkelers to the best vantage points to witness these magnificent creatures up close.

While Manta Bay in Nusa Penida is undoubtedly a highlight for snorkelers in Bali, it is crucial to remember the importance of responsible tourism and marine conservation. Snorkelers should respect the marine environment by maintaining a safe distance from the marine life, refraining from touching or feeding them, and avoiding any contact with coral or other fragile underwater structures. By adhering to these guidelines, visitors can contribute to the preservation of Bali's extraordinary marine ecosystem.

Snorkeling in Bali's Manta Bay is an experience that leaves an indelible impression on the hearts and minds of those fortunate enough to witness it. The combination of the stunning natural beauty, the awe-inspiring presence of manta rays, and the vibrant underwater world of Nusa Penida creates a truly unforgettable adventure. So, grab your snorkeling gear and dive into the waters of Manta Bay for an enchanting encounter with these majestic creatures in the breathtaking island paradise of Bali.

Our day wise recommendations:
Day 1: 
Explore Kuta in the evening, the local markets, local streets. Have a beach walk on kuta beach in the evening to have a look at beautiful sunset.

After sunset you can go to "Kuta beachwalk mall" which is along the kuta beach coastline, explore some branded shops.

You can have dinner at nightclubs near your property, there are plenty of them,

Day 2:
When in Bali, we recommend you to start your day as early as possible, to avoid long queues and traffic at most of the places, though we understand it is difficult to rise early in the morning when you are gone for honeymoon 😉.
You can start your day 2 by visiting World's tallest Garuda statue and the statue that you would be able to see from almost whole of Bali's plains.
We are talking about "Garuda Wisnu Cultural Park"

You can visit this place on day 2 in Bali, and there's a whole lot of experience waiting for you at this place, and if you would even start here after breakfast at your property, you would still be able to spend some quality time here together.

Stay there till 3 or 4 in the evening, and then leave for Uluwatu temple, which has a breathtaking view along with a stunning sunset.

After sunset come down from the Uluwatu cliff and you would find:
- The Ritual Bali
- O Uluwatu Nightclub
- Single Fin Bali
- Mana Uluwatu

Day 3:
Planning for third day requires some time in the morning in day 2 to book Nusa Penida Day tour from Kuta's local market

Nusa Penida Travel Guide for Nusa Penida Day Trip
https://youtu.be/wTKhojxy1fs

Nusa Penida is an exotic place, another island beside Bali. It's a complete picturesque package and a perk for Instagram pictures and reels.

We suggest you to spend your whole day 3 at Nusa Penida, to experience the surreal Balinese and Indonesian adventure.

Day 4:
After a whole day of island hopping and travelling, we suggest you to go slow on day 4 and relax.

You can start your day with Tanah Lot Temple in the morning, and then spend the rest of the day at Seminyak in beachclubs like Finns, Potato head or Ku de ta. 

Ku De Ta Beach Club | Ku De Ta Seminyak Bali | Unsponsored Review | Bali Vlog
https://youtu.be/avppL2wirmU

Seminyak is one of the busiest places of Bali, and has a flea market to explore too.

Day 5:
Move to Ubud, as travelling from south of Bali to the rest of it will not be possible from south Bali everyday.

Ubud has waterfalls, mountains, forests, temples, and what not to explore..

List of Waterfalls to explore:
1. Tegenungan Waterfall
2. Tibumana Waterfall
3. Nungnung Waterfall
4. Kanto Lampo Waterfall

You can also explore Monkey forest, but keeping in mind the honeymoon specific itinerary we haven't added it to the list

Temples to explore:
1. Goa Gajah Temple
2. Pura Taman Saraswati
3. Pura Tirta Empul

Don't forget to experience the Balinese Massage & Spa in your property.
You can try doing it on last day also.

Are you planning a trip to Ubud, Bali, Indonesia and wondering what to do? In this 4K Bali travel guide, we take you through a 3-day Ubud travel itinerary, packed with must-visit locations, cultural gems, and breathtaking landscapes. From the sacred Tirta Empul holy spring to the stunning bali rice fields ubud, we cover everything you need to make your trip unforgettable.

Start your adventure at the holy springs of Tirta Empul, one of Bali’s most sacred water temples. Experience a traditional purification ritual and immerse yourself in the spiritual energy of this warisan budaya Bali (Balinese cultural heritage). Then, head to the world-famous Bali rice terrace swing, where you can capture breathtaking views of Bali rice fields Ubud while soaring over lush landscapes when you walk through the tegallalang rice terraces Bali Indonesia.

No visit to Ubud is complete without exploring Goa Gajah Bali Indonesia, also known as the Elephant Caves of Bali. This ancient temple, part of wisata Goa Gajah, is a significant historical and spiritual site. Stroll through the mystical carvings and discover the serene atmosphere that makes this temple so unique.

Another must-see is Pura Gunung Kawi Ubud, a breathtaking temple complex carved into the cliffs. Walk through lush rice terraces and descend the stone steps to witness these ancient royal shrines, surrounded by tranquil nature. This hidden gem is one of Bali’s most awe-inspiring archaeological sites.

Take in the beauty of Ubud by walking along Ubud streets, where you’ll find vibrant markets, local crafts, and authentic Balinese culture. Visit the famous Ubud Market to shop for handcrafted souvenirs and traditional art, then step into the majestic Ubud Palace to admire its stunning architecture.

For nature lovers, embark on the Campuhan Ridge Walk Ubud, one of the most scenic beautiful hikes in Ubud. This ridge walk Bali offers breathtaking views of rolling hills, lush greenery, and tranquil surroundings. The Ubud Ridge Walk is the perfect way to escape the busy streets and reconnect with nature.

End your adventure with a visit to Monkey Forest Bali Ubud, where you can see playful macaques in their natural habitat, surrounded by towering trees and ancient temple ruins. Whether you’re looking for adventure, culture, or relaxation, this Ubud travel itinerary has it all.

It's best to arrive just before sunrise, since the lighting will be best and you'll have the fields to yourself before they get crowded with tourists.

You can access the rice fields easily from a few entrances right along the street.
Just follow the signs that say "trekking," and you may or may not have to pay a nominal fee to enter.

The stone paths become muddy walkways through the fields, and especially in the mornings you'll encounter local farmers tending to the crops.

The complex irrigation system helped the Tegalalang Rice Terraces gain its UNESCO World Heritage Site designation.

fb_RqPWfSZo.description:
In this Indonesia Travel Vlog, we decided to sign up for a tour to go snorkeling with manta rays in Nusa Penida! In our last video we were able to watch people snorkeling with mantas from the Manta View cliff and it looked amazing! We decided that we really wanted to experience this for ourselves! We found a tour close to the pier in Nusa Penida that was 200,000 Rp each ($13.23 USD). There were two options: a morning tour or an afternoon tour. As we already had plans in the morning, we decided to do the afternoon tour at 2pm. We met at the place where we paid for the tour and they drove us to the pier where we joined many other people who were on the same tour. The tour was supposed to stop at 4 points (Manta Bay, Cristal Bay, Gamat Bay, and Toya Pakeh Point). We ended up only going to 3 of the 4 stops as some people on the tour had to catch the ferry back to mainland Bali. We were also confused as the tour we did didn't go to the same Manta Point that we had seen from the cliff. Apparently there is more than one location for the manta rays. We drove about 20 minutes to the first stop and the guys in charge told us that instead of manta rays there were wild dolphins! They said that manta rays are scared of dolphins, so the mantas would have left, but we were able to jump in and see over 10 wild dolphins! It was amazing even to see them so close to the boat! Then we drove just a couple minutes away to the second stop where there were two manta rays! We were able to snorkel very close to them which was so amazing! They are so huge and they glide through the water unlike anything we've ever seen! Unfortunately at one point Carles got stung by a jellyfish! Luckily the guys on the boat had something to put on it to stop it from stinging so much. We then went to the final location were there were lots of colorful fish in the water. It ended up being such a great trip and we are still amazed by the manta rays and dolphins! (If you do a manta ray snorkel tour, try to go in the morning as they said they saw many more manta rays in the morning than in the afternoon)!

hrA4ZebPGn8.description:
In this video I am gonna tell you why you should not hike Mount Batur in Bali. People do not share the reality of this place and I am here to do so.

This is the most known hike in the island and many people share this as being a magical and life changing experience but they forget to share the problems of this hike. Mount Batur is considered sacred to the locals and they use this as an excuse to treat this place as the most commercial hike I have ever seen.

They tell you It is mandatory to hike with a guide and pay the entrance fee. If you ask them anything about it or try to hike without a guide they become agressive, sometimes even physically like with my boyfriend (he was just asking how it worked). They will tell you wrong directions of the trail and much more.

They say they do it because of the sacredness of the mountain but what they are doing is basically turning Mount Batur into a commercial site where you don't see or feel the real sacredness at all.

The hike is packed. You are with more than a thousand people in an endless line going up to the volcano. The quietness, contact with nature and calm that you usually get from a hike are interrupted by all the groups with loud music, locals trying to sell their stuff and being pushy. Renting blankets, bracelets, food. It is basically a mall on a mountain.

I am happy to pay for entrance fees, guide if necessary or anything like that if it is being done in a fair and proper way where they actually protect the sacredness that they talk so much about. Where they actually protect nature, clean the mountain which also does not happen.

The Best being: Manta Point, SD, Mangrove, Blue Corner, Toyapakeh.

Possibly five of the best dive sites in South-Eastern Bali.

Manta Point speaks for itself. It's one of the few places where you can (almost) guarantee a close encounter. SD and Mangrove have a nearly unrivalled abundance of reef fish and beautiful corals.  10 Things to know before you visit Bali ✨
✨ Visa is on arrival for Indians for USD 35. Preferable to carry USD cash. RT PCR is not required for fully vaccinated Indians.

✨Travel insurance for 10 days trip costs about ₹800 pp.
.
✨ There are no direct flights to Bali from India. Flight tickets can get VERY expensive so book in advance.
.
✨Cash is king.Islands like Nusa Penida COMPLETELY rely on Cash.Currency is Indonesian Rupiah (IDR).
1 INR = 187 IDR (approx)
1 USD = 14800 IDR (approx)
.
✨ Bali has tropical weather in most parts. Northern Bali can get chilly.Best time to visit is between May- October. Wet season starts thereafter.
.

✨ Bali is HUGE. To get from one place to another can take very long & there’s no public transport. Roads are narrow and traffic can be crazy in peak hours. Always keep buffer time and travel. 🕰️
.
✨ Grab & Gojek are you go to for internal transfers by cab. Renting a bike is the easiest way to go around. Scooter rental costs anywhere between IDR 70k to IDR 100k (₹350-₹500) per day.
.
✨Nusa Penida and Nusa Lembongan HAVE ONE OF THE BEST REEFS IN THE WORLD. Must go snorkelling here. Costs about 200k IDR (₹1000)
.
✨Bali swing is WORTH the hype. ATV ride and River Rafting are incredible & can be done at very affordable prices in Ubud. (₹4000 pp)
.
✨Avoid street food from very small stalls. Avoid drinking water outside. Prefer to purchase sealed water bottles. FOOD HERE IS DELICIOUS. Must try the Chicken & Lamb Satay♥️
.
Save & share with your Bali gang now.
.

We're leaving Bali and taking a fast boat ferry to reach Gili Trawangan in the Gili Islands. You can read some pretty bad things online, so we booked Ekajaya ferry to see if it's... Book your ferry here: https://geni.us/giliferry ⬇ Other Bali recommendations are below ⬇  

The time has come to leave Bali and head to the AWESOME Gili Islands... which, a lot of travellers don't actually realise are part of Lombok, not Bali. Either way, I've been to the Gili Islands once before (Dane, about 12 years ago) and loved it - so I always wanted to get back to Gili Trawangan and explore Gili Air as well with Stace eventually.

BUT, the big issue is with the fast boat ferries. There's some shocking reviews online, along with some very sad stories recently, so it's kind of difficult to know which is the best way to get from Bali to the Gili Islands and which is the best ferry. After loads of research we thought Eka Jaya was going to be the best - it's the largest boat, which does mean it's a bit slower, but it seemed a bit safer to us. 

In this vlog we go through the process of seeing just how crap these fast boat ferries are and honestly, it wasn't nearly as bad as we thought. Going over was smooth sailing, coming back, not so much as we sat around waiting for the boat and then had a weird sea transfer. It's a small price to pay for the beauty and relaxing on the Gili Islands though - so check back for those vlogs next time.

Gili Trawangan -- Bali's ultimate party island, where there isn't a single car or scooter!  In this video I'm showing you the real party side of Gili T, exactly how to get here from Bali, and how to explore the whole island — all in one guide.

How to get to Gili Trawangan from Bali?

Fastest option: fast boat from Padang Bai (~1.5 hours). Boats also run from Serangan, Sanur and Nusa Dua. There are no direct flights. Tip: take a morning boat — the sea is calmest then. Port tax is often not included in the ticket, so carry some cash at the harbour.

Book your speedboat tickets from klook at get an 10% discount by using my code "chaloletsgo" at checkout here: https://s.klook.com/c/mXYg4EOdw2

Rent a bicycle (~IDR 50–75k/day) or take a cidomo (horse cart)
Snorkel at Turtle Point — turtles almost guaranteed

3-island snorkeling tour (Trawangan + Meno + Air)

n9lMh4wFzjk.description:
North Bali, Indonesia is famous for  hills, rice terraces, waterfalls and is largely popular for peace and greenery & cold weather. 

We did a Day trip to North Bali and visited a couple of sightseeing locations like Leke Leke water falls, Jatiluwih rice terrace, Fruit and vegetables market and Handara gate.

We started early morning at around 8 am from Ubud, Central Bali  and reached Ubud by end of the day.

i would suggest you to plan one night stay in North Bali for a better experience.

Date of Journey - 19th March 2024 
Driver- Dewa  we did only first and last day with him, on rest days his brother in law was there
Dewa number - +62 818-569-293

Just in case if you have missed watching our previous BTS episodes of how we reach Bali, Indonesia. You may check the video on the below link 

EP - 1 BTS Delhi to Bangkok - https://youtu.be/w7I_HyRfQ1E

EP - 2 Bangkok to Bali - https://youtu.be/GUXBoPssY7s

Below are the Activities we did throughout the day.

Leke Leke Waterfalls - We traveled around 30 km from the Ubud & started our day in the morning from Leke Leke Falls. After some Stairs going down, we reached the falls & we enjoyed bathing in the Fall, overall it was a great experience here.

Leke Leke Waterfalls Tickets - IDR - 50,000
                              INR - 260 ( Approx )

Waterfall Timing - 7:00 am to 5:30 pm

Jatiluwh Rice Terrace - After this, we traveled around 20 km and reached the World Heritage Site “Jatiluwh Rice Terrace”& saw the amazing view of Rice Terrace there. This Rice field is about Organic farming which is one of the reasons it’s considered a World Heritage Site.

Red Rice Local Shop - After this, we visited the local shop there & tasted the Snake fruit, & We also purchased Red Rice from there.

Red Rice Cost - 15,000 IDR 
                           Rs 80 INR approx

Coconut Water - After some Trek we bought Coconut water & enjoyed the rice terrace view while having it.

Coconut Water Cost - 10,000 IDR 
                                    110 INR approx

Warung near Jatiluwih rice terrace - Then we found an eatery and had their Balinese Cake which is a combination of Red Rice, Sticky Rice, avocado & Palm Sugar.

Lunch at Nadi Resort - After this, we travelled around 10 km and reached the Nadi Resort & had lunch there overall the lunch was great in taste & environment of the resort was also so nice.
Tariff of room at this resort is about 100 USD which includes breakfast.

Lunch Cost - Moong Dal - 1, 70,000 IDR (  INR - 880 )
                    Baingan Bharta - 95,000 IDR ( INR - 450 ) 

Fruit & Vegetable Market - After lunch we visited the Fruit & Vegetable Market & explored the different types of fruits there & tasted the Snow fruit & Mangosteen which i hadn’t tasted it before.

Ulun Danu Beratan Temple - Then we travelled around 10 mins from the fruit market & reached at the Ulun Danu Temple. This is the Lord Shiva Temple. The temple complex is on the shores of Lake Beratan. This temple was built in 1633, & the temple is a mixture of Hinduism and Buddhism

Temple Ticket - IDR - 75,000 ( INR 390 ) Per Person

Handara Gate - After this, we visited the Handara Gate, known as the Gate of Heaven Bali. The gate with its stunning Architecture & picturesque surroundings this place is the perfect spot for capturing amazing photographs. We also took some great Photographs here.

Handara Gate Ticket - IDR 50,000 ( INR 260 ) Per Person

After this, we ended our day 

Hope you enjoyed this “North Bali” Episode

qm7D7qijlAo.description:
Asking locals on Bali, many will tell you: Banyumala and Sekumpul are two of the most beautiful.  You can check out a full list and map here:

https://www.jaredsdetours.com/bali-waterfalls/

In this video, you'll see:
1.  Leke Leke, about an hour's drive from Ubud.
After the relatively easy hike in, you can cool off by swimming in the pool at the waterfall's base.

2.  Goa Raja, which is is one of our favorite waterfalls on Bali.
After a pretty easy hike, you'll walk around giant stone walls and find a powerful waterfall inside.  It almost creates its own weather system inside the cave.
Just outside is a gorgeous waterfall, which cascades into a manmade pool.  

3.  You'll find Tukad Cepung at the end of a cavernous hike through a gorge.
It's a favorite for photographers, as the sunlight creates different scenes inside as it passes during the day.

4.  You'll likely find a bigger crowd at Kanto Lampo.
It's another "wait your turn for a photo" site.

5.  I'd also recommend going to see this smaller waterfall, tucked away in the corner of the Tagalalang Rice Terraces.
You'll have to hike the dirt paths through the rice fields, but the views are stunning, and the waterfall and irrigation system helped the site gain its UNESCO World Heritage Site designation.  

6. Tibumana is popular, and is a decent spot for swimming.

7.  Taman Sari is nearby, and another good swimming hole.  The two-tiered waterfall is pretty, but it doesn't compare in my mind to some of the others.

8.  Taman Beji Griya is another I'd skip.
The waterfalls here are beautiful, but for me it's too much of a commercialized spiritual site… almost like the ceremonies were created for social media experiences.

9.  If you have time to island-hop, I'd definitely spend time on East Java, taking the lengthy but worthwhile trip to Tempak Sewu.

🌴 Welcome back to Bali Vlog 6! Today we dive into one of the most unforgettable experiences of our entire trip — Snorkelling in Nusa Penida! 🐠🌊

We're staying at Devi’s Sun Sun Beach Hotel, right next to the beautiful Sun Sun Beach 🏖️, and from here we booked our snorkelling adventure for just IDR 500K (≈ ₹2,659 / ~USD 32). No third-party agents, no hidden charges — just direct hotel booking for the cheapest & safest experience!

🌊 ✨ Snorkelling Spots We Covered Today

🥇 1️⃣ MANTA POINT – Home of the Majestic Manta Rays
This is the MOST iconic snorkelling spot in Bali!
Here you can witness huge, graceful Manta Rays gliding around you. The water is deep with 10–20m visibility — perfect for spotting mantas from a safe distance.
📌 Highlight: Once-in-a-lifetime chance to swim above manta rays!

🥈 2️⃣ CRYSTAL BAY – Clearest Water + Colourful Corals
Famous for its super clear water and vibrant reef system, Crystal Bay offers tropical fish, soft corals & sometimes sea turtles!
📌 Highlight: 30m visibility, perfect for GoPro footage & cinematic shots.

🥉 3️⃣ SD POINT – The Smooth Drift Snorkelling Experience
Located on the north coast, SD Point gives you a relaxing “glide along the reef” experience.
You float & the gentle current takes you forward — you see endless coral gardens, schools of fish & colourful marine life everywhere.
📌 Highlight: Massive reef wall + calming drift snorkelling!

⭐ PRICE BREAKDOWN
• Snorkelling Package: 500K IDR
• Indian Rupees: ₹2,659
• US Dollars: ~USD 32
This included:
✔️ Boat pickup
✔️ Full snorkelling gear
✔️ Guide
✔️ Water & safety briefing

🚤 HOW TO BOOK (Cheapest Method)

💡 Best Tip: Book directly from your hotel (like I did).
No third-party agents, no online markup.
Hotel wale local operators se tied up hote hain, so price lowest milta hai.

🧭 Do’s & Don’ts for Snorkelling

✅ DO’S
✔️ Wear life jacket always
✔️ Follow your guide — currents can be strong
✔️ Use reef-safe sunscreen
✔️ Stay calm & float if you're a beginner
✔️ Keep a waterproof camera ready — marine life is INSANE

❌ DON’TS
✘ Corals ko touch mat karo — bahut fragile hote hain
✘ Manta Rays ke too close mat jao
✘ Propellers ke near snorkel mat karo
✘ Panic mat karo — guides trained hote hain

🌟 PRO TIPS (Must Read!)

💡 Best Time: Morning (calmer water + better visibility)
💡 Gear Check: Mask tight fit honi chahiye, else fogging/backwash hota hai
💡 Don’t Eat Heavy: Seasickness common hota hai
💡 Carry: Dry bag, towel, GoPro, water bottle

tl3u8IqPBZY.description:
After Exploring Ubud, Bali, We travelled to  Nusa Penida Island in Indonesia.  Just in case if you have missed watching previous episode.

EP - 4 Ubud -  https://youtu.be/UuMxLPGGbIU?si=cnxt2kORDwf83pQO

Below are the Activities we did throughout the day.

Kelingking Beach Sunset - Here we experienced a beautiful sunset from the viewpoint & it was such a great experience.

Here you can also go down to the beach by stairs which takes around 1 hour to get there, we skipped to go there. 

Nusa Majesty Bungalow - After this, we reached our Hotel in Nusa Penida, we stayed at “Nusa Majesty Bungalow” which was suggested by our driver Mr. Teddy & it’s in the Central location so it would be easy for us.

Stay at this hotel was average, this small hotel lacks staff, so its like 1 person giving service to all the rooms in the hotel.

Hotel Tariff - IDR - 3,60,000 (1,850 INR) for double occupancy including breakfast for March month.

Dinner at Bollywood Cuisine Restaurant - After this we had our dinner at Bollywood Cuisine Restaurant, It’s an Indian Restaurant. We had Paneer Tikka Masala & Mix Veg.

Nusa Majesty Bungalow and Bollywood cuisine restaurant is adjacent to each other.

Dinner Cost - Paneer Tikka Masala - 1,15,000 IDR (INR 600)
Mix Veg - 98,000 IDR (INR 510)

After this, we ended our day 1 in Nusa Penida

Next Morning 24th March

Angel’s Billabong Beach - Angel's Billabong and Broken beach are 200 meters away from each other.

We also saw a beautiful view of Broken Beach from the big mountain & the view was really amazing to see.

Coconut Water - After this we had a refreshing Coconut Water to beat the heat of the Islands 

Coconut water Price - 25,000 IDR (INR 130)

Crystal Bay Beach - After this, we travelled around 15 km and reached Crystal Bay Beach here also the beach was very clean with an amazing view.

Lunch near Crystal Beach - After this we had our lunch near Crystal Beach we had a Chicken Sandwich & grilled Fish in the lunch. There are many shacks at the crystal beach.

Lunch Cost - Chicken Sandwich - 50,000 IDR (260 INR)
Grilled Fish - 70,000 IDR (360 INR)

Snorkeling at Banjar Nyuh Harbour - After this, we traveled around 10 km from Crystal Beach & reached at Banjar Nyuh Harbour for snorkeling, We decided to go for a private boat. Which included 3 places for Snorkelling - Manta Bay, Gamat Point & SD Point 

Snorkeling Cost at Sharing - Rs 2500 Approx
Snorkelling Cost Private Boat - Rs 8,500

Person who assisted us for the snorkelling is actually a office staff, he does not usually go out with the customers. Other filed staff was average, so i will suggest you to try out some other operator for snorkellling.

Manta Bay - Our first point of Snorkelling was “Manta Bay” Here people come to see the Manta Ray fish and fortunately we saw the fish from very close distance during the snorkeling.

Chances of seeing Manta Ray are less, though people plan this activity with hope to see Manta Ray.
Gamat Point - After this, we did the snorkelling at the 2nd point here the depth of the water was a little less. we saw here the different kinds of fish under the water.

SD Point - After 15 mins of Boat ride we did the Snorkelling at the 3rd point known as Gamat Point.

Overall the Snorkelling experience was good we enjoyed a lot.

Hotel near Diamond Beach - After we reached our Hotel we booked our accommodation at Lempeh Jungle Cottage near Diamond Beach.
Next day we wanted to see Sunrise at Diamond beach so thought of changing hotel location and moved to this hotel.

Hotel Tariff - Rs 2,100 for double occupancy including breakfast for March month 

Hotel name - Lempeh jungle cottage.

After this we ended our 2nd day in Nusa Penida

Next Day Morning – 25th March 

Sunrise at Diamond Beach - In the Morning at 5 am we reached Diamond Beach to see the beautiful Sunrise. It was a really great experience to see the Sunrise here.

After this, we ended our Nusa Penida Tour.

We paid him 12k in Indian currency for two half days and one full day.( Payment was done in IDR only) but this estimate is post conversion.

Info regarding Gilli island.

If from Sanur to Nusa Penida from Nusa Penida to Gili Terawangan, every day there are 5 fast boat companies leaving at 8.30 am and 9 am from Sanur port.   the name theree angle trip.  Travel duration is approximately 4 hours from Sanur to Gili.  You can buy tickets online or through a tour agent and buy directly at the port.

But it is more popular via Padang Bai port if you want to go to Gili - from Gili to -  Penida -  to Sanur.  because the duration of the journey is approximately 2 hours from Padang Bai port to Gili.  There are 10 company fast boats serving visitors if they want to cross.  starting at 8.30 am until the last fast boat is at 2.30 pm.  buy tickets online and buy them directly at the ticket counter there.

Thanks
Harish Bali

Top 5️⃣ Things to Do for Families in Bali 🌺🌴

Here are some of our favorite family-friendly activities in Bali:

1️⃣ Bali Zoo 🦁: Spend a day at Bali Zoo where you can get up close and personal with a variety of animals. From interactive feeding sessions to night safaris, there's something exciting for everyone!

2️⃣ Campuhan Ridge Walk 🌄: This picturesque walk offers stunning views of Ubud's lush landscapes. It's a great way to enjoy the natural beauty of Bali while getting some exercise. Don't forget to bring your camera!

3️⃣ Monkey Forest Sanctuary 🐒: Located in the heart of Ubud, this sanctuary is home to hundreds of playful monkeys. Explore the beautiful forest and ancient temples, but be sure to keep a close eye on your belongings!

4️⃣ Jinenku Day Club 🏊: Take a break and relax at Jinenku Day Club. Enjoy a pool day with the family, complete with great food, refreshing drinks, and a stunning setting. It’s the perfect way to unwind!

5️⃣ GWK Cultural Park 🎭: Immerse yourself in Balinese culture at GWK Cultural Park. See the massive Garuda Wisnu Kencana statue, enjoy traditional dance performances, and learn about the rich cultural heritage of Bali.

INSIDER TIP: Make sure to visit these spots early in the day to avoid the crowds and enjoy a more relaxed experience.

vMjTrjbW_oA.description:
If this is your first time travelling to Bali, Indonesia well we got you! Stay tuned for part 2.

1) Visa on Arrival will cost IDR500,000 
You can pay with cash or credit card at Ngurah Rai Bali International Airport. No need to apply visa for tourist before you travel, this visa on arrival will allow you to stay up to 30 Days. 

2) Get connected with e-Sim or Sim card
You can purchase the tourist sim card at the airport itself and we recommend Telkomsel as great internet provider from local pov. E-sim card is also convenient as you don't need to get the physical sim card.

3) Download Gojek or Grab application
Taxi is expensive in Bali and it's quite hard to find in some places unless you make a call to book. Note a lot of sim card for tourist does not give you any credit to make phone call but only internet. Hence it is important to get connected so you can download these two apps. They are also cheaper than taxi in general and really convenient. Tips: download these two apps BEFORE you come to Bali to load your credit or debit card details.

zeIEh8HnATU.description:
Snorkeling or Diving at manta point nusa penida is just amazing. Are you doubting about manta bay vs manta point? I would personally pick manta point.

You should go to manta point nusa penida. It has a high population of manta rays. The earlier in the morning you go the more manta rays you'll see at manta point nusa penida. We went at 08:00 AM and we saw more than 20 manta rays. I've done snorkeling and manta point diving here. Both are great!

The reason I recommend manta point nusa penida over manta bay is because at manta bay chances are lower to see mantas and you'll mostly see only 1-2 small ones. At manta point the manta rays are giants and you'll have a big chance of seeing up to 20 mantas with sometimes more than 10 together.

If you like ocean videos make sure to subscribe and like! And I'll see you next time!
